steps.text: The Cautus has never thought that oncoming doom, especially one pressing down on their neck, could be something to be accepted calmly.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I-I could never be so indifferent if I had to live through everyone and everything I love being destroyed.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I don't understand how you—

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: It's not indifference, but instead a belief in the absolute equality of the universe. It's a shame you arrived just a little bit late.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: This ship had just encountered a star going supernova several thousand light-years away and made a smooth withdrawal.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: If you see that sight with your own eyes, perhaps you will understand my meaning.
The instruments in the hall begin to spin rapidly, until they are moving too fast for the Cautus to see with the naked eye.
Then, she sees a multitude of lights and shadows appear and float through the air.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I see a giant sphere emitting a deep, dark red light, and a small indigo dot speeding across its surface.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: But... it seems like it's the big sphere rotating around the blue dot?

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: The one you call the 'blue dot' is the pulsar that just went supernova I mentioned.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: The red star which is gradually being torn apart is its partner, now doomed to die as well.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: They once harbored many interesting primitive lifeforms. I have many fond memories of wandering through the planets of that star system.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: It's a pity they were snuffed out before they could see the world beyond the sky.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...Why are you showing this to me?

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: Simply sharing the knowledge we have with you, traveler.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: One-sided paranoia and ignorance are often barriers to effective information transfer. I have no knowledge of your history, either.
The Cautus has barely had the time to comprehend these words before suddenly, her newly-acquired knowledge begins to assault her mind.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: The land... may see life be born twice? These stars fallen from the sky... can harbor life of their own?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Ruination's end... is not despair.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: We're... not special, when it comes to the land?

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: A celestial body that can sustain life loves all that live upon it equally, no matter where they hail from. This is a law of nature.

steps.name: Mysterious Elf
steps.text: Don't be too greedy in lapping up that knowledge you can't fully understand yet.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I saw you among all that information. You once had many of your people by your side, but suddenly—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: 'The Presence'. That's what a lot of people call you, right?

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: I am just a wandering presence, true. Like I said, when true destruction bore down on me and my fellows, I was powerless.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...What exactly is this destruction you keep talking about?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I've seen plenty of things here I can only describe as 'divine acts'. What could possibly threaten people like you?

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: I'm afraid that nobody on this ship can answer your question, traveler.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: In your eyes, we possess knowledge that many lifeforms in this universe would consider 'divine acts'...

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: But in this boundless cosmos, even we have limits to what we can explore and investigate.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: Are you disappointed?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: So there's definitely no eternal kingdom, a paradise where everyone can experience endless joy and happiness?

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: Would you like such a place to exist?
The Cautus hesitates for a moment before nodding.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: Nothing lives forever. Looking back through the history I know, I have come across legendary civilizations that have conquered countless star systems, spreading across the cosmos for millions of years.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: But as far as the universe cares, what they left behind was, in the end, utterly insignificant.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: We once blindly chased after non-existent principles and ideals... In the midst of that golden age beyond recollection, we believed our existences to have a sure purpose.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: But in the end?

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: Any lifeform born with intelligence insists on declaring itself the center of its world, but whether or not it is right, in the universe's eyes—

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: From start to finish, we are nothing. This is the first thing you must learn before you can understand it.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: Remember that brilliant supernova you just saw?

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: From that tomb, life will be born anew, and there will come a day when those beings will understand what we have carved on our grave.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: That we once had lives of our own. That we existed.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...I don't understand anything that you're saying.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: How were we born on this land?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Was there an even more glorious civilization here before us?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Are we going to be wiped out in the foreseeable future?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: But what I really want to know is, all this pain and suffering that Originium brings with it... Can it be eliminated?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I beg you, show me the way to the answers I seek...

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: I can't answer any of your questions. Your first three have been asked in a myriad of languages in a myriad of ways across the universe. Only you can answer them yourself.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: As for your final question... I'm terribly sorry, but I've never heard of this 'Originium', and I can't find anything related to it in our databases.

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: However, I do know someone rather interesting, who also happens to be the master of this ship. Perhaps she will be able to solve your riddle.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: The master of this ship?

steps.name: The Presence
steps.text: She's a linguist of wide renown. Her name is—
'Priestess'.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No time to be lost in your thoughts, Doctor!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Grab onto me!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I can't break my focus right now. Weaving together a way to the singularity is incredibly difficult.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Even if Theresa were here to help...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Did you see something, Doctor?!
You see a familiar figure.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I will! I'm doing everything I can right now to stabilize the connection points, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa has marked all the records Dr. Kal'tsit searched through earlier. I'm trying to link them all together.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But I still need an anchor point, one that can guide me back—

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I will keep watch here, and serve as your anchor.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Press onwards, Amiya.
Pink, silken threads begin to gather.
The meandering threads interweave and spiral, gradually spreading out from the boundary into the distance.
Beyond its walls, the path to the singularity slowly takes shape.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's working!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Originium Arts don't seem to work here, but applying the logic behind casting them to the information here does!

options: Can you build the 'bridge' using completely unknown information?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, this place is full of information I can't analyze, not even with the help of Civilight Eterna. I wouldn't have been able to make this way forward alone.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But thankfully, Dr. Kal'tsit's access left records, and with Theresa's help, I can grasp onto her research data.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That's more than enough for me.
The pink threads continue to slowly spiral, linking together the many pieces of complex data that Kal'tsit left her mark on.
String by interwoven string, the path forward gradually forms.

a.text: 'I can tell how you're feeling, Kal'tsit.'

'By analyzing the emotional matrix I constructed of you without your permission, I see your tenseness is not only because of my sharing an appearance with Theresa. You have something even heavier on your mind.'
'I will try to adjust. I don't want my personal emotional changes to interfere with the objectivity of those who come after me when they query these records.'
'Yet they are still changing, Kal'tsit. Are you afraid?'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's not the most efficient way to build a bridge, but it should hold.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm going to try to get closer to the singularity.

a.text: 'I'm afraid Amiya and the Doctor won't be able to find the information I leave behind, and I'm afraid...'
'That if the situation worsens to the point that they are forced to take such extreme measures, the trail I cleared for them would no longer be of use...'
'Or that I might mistakenly lead these seekers of knowledge towards a threat I dare not speak of.'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, Doctor. I won't let you, not before I check its condition myself.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Sorry, I know I'm being stubborn about it, but this is my decision.
The bridge, formed from countless strands of entwined information, stretches out into the distance to touch upon the singularity.
Without the slightest hesitation, Amiya steps onto it, her first step outside the walls of the boundary—
A surge.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This feeling, it's like the information has formed some sort of great wave. But why—

options: This is only the beginning, I'm afraid.
'The closer you get to the singularity, the denser the information will become.'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It really is like Theresa said. The information here has mass.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We'll most likely find greater resistance the deeper we go.

options: We need to come up with a better plan.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I can't maintain the stability of a bridge this weak. Going this deep has taken a greater toll than I expected.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I need to keep going forward. As long as I follow Dr. Kal'tsit's beacons...
The silver mountains the Teekaz had entered flit by her; the black shadow cast by the Feranmut plunging into icefield vanished momentarily.
She sees more scenes fly past her, as if she were fighting the current of the river of time.
More and more incomprehensible, indescribable sights assail her mind.
She does her best to block out the unending, chaotic stream of information.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Concentrate, Amiya, concentrate... Just keep focusing on Dr. Kal'tsit's beacons... Press onwards...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I just need to touch the singularity—
Silence.
Amiya cannot even hear her own breathing.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What... is this place?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That giant sphere... is disintegrating?
Looking at the shattered sphere makes her feel dizzy, but it is the bizarrely-shaped ship floating in the air that causes an even greater bout of lightheadedness.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What... is going on?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Why am I seeing—
As she is trapped in her spell of dizziness, a rotating boulder slowly but inexorably hurtles towards her.
Its black shadow quickly fills Amiya's vision. She subconsciously tries to defend herself, but it is immediately followed by the feeling of freefall.
Did she fail...? Was it a surge of information?
'Amiya!'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Doctor...?
Amiya senses a hand supporting her, keeping her thoughts steady by bracing her.

options: Try to block out the interfering information.
Sorry, I couldn't sit back and do as I was told.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor... Thank goodness...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That moment just now...
You do your best to support her shaking body as the information wave surging from the singularity continues its assault.
The information, so dense it has nearly taken true shape, washes over your thoughts, leaving behind jumbled afterimages in the void—
It is the past long gone, the present being recorded en masse, and what seems to be the future, foreseeing your next steps.
It's a shame that right now, you do not have energy to spare to pay it any heed.
The two of you have already made the long, long, long trek from the boundary to this point without even noticing, and now, the singularity...
The singularity is right in front of you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Did you see that terrifying scene earlier, Doctor?

options: I don't know what it means, though.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm certain it's not something that took place on Terra...

options: But at least it means we're getting close to the singularity.
Even more information will show itself to us.
Can you still keep going, Amiya?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Y-Yes, yes I can.
You are well aware of the situation you are in right now. Despite knowing it will have minimal effect, you still subconsciously stretch out your arm to try and shield Amiya.

options: The attacks here are focused on our thoughts. I can handle it.
I've got a lead on what we're here for.
I've run the calcs on Kal'tsit's access records.
You can read the key points from my mind.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Found them.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Using 'Slumber Bridge' as a filter, Dr. Kal'tsit conducted a total of 79,346 searches...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Although all the searches are related to 'Originium', according to your speculation, this data is not strongly related to its actual essential nature.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If the results are restricted and give us nothing, doesn't the trail run cold here?

options: Kal'tsit retrieved the same entry over and over again.
This is, in itself, some information for us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: A repeated retrieval? Wait, can the infinitely-looping code made from the repeat query count be deciphered too?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...You already know the answer, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I've never heard of this name. Neither you nor Dr. Kal'tsit has ever said it before—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: 'Priestess'?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: —Doctor, are you seeing what I'm seeing?
'Priestess...'
You have never seen this scene before, much less seen—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) You're here, {@nickname}.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: (Unknown language) It took some time to refine your design for PRTS.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: (Unknown language) I thought you had gone to take a rest.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) No, I've been thinking about your words this whole time.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) 'There is no language that can describe God, as the existence of God itself cannot be understood.'

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: (Unknown language) You know that was just mindless chatter.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) Suppose I take it as an axiom.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) With it as my starting point, would creating a language that can describe God mean we have the means to understand It?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) Does the prospect not excite you?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) Perhaps, in the pursuit of the answer to this question, we have been going down the wrong path—trying to understand the nature of the universe with its own laws.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: (Unknown language) You want to use a language wholly created by us to interpret the universe. A far too audacious idea, Priestess.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) Haha, is it?
Without any further hesitation, she traces out a perfect rhombus in the air.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: (Unknown language) Let's begin, shall we?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What are they discussing, Doctor?
You have seen this woman before in the Assimilated Universe. She once accompanied you—

a.text: That when you are truly confused by everything, you will remember: the answers you seek were here all along.
